Basic Assessment: A Step-by-Step Guide

Easy_Example.Rmd

Getting Started with a Basic Assessment

This guide walks through a Basic Assessment for mature dairy cattle in Spain (2015), using a single national-level identifier to link census data, nutrition, and environmental impact from start to finish.

📂 All files referenced below live in user_data/ and correspond to the pre-configured inst/Examples/Level1_Spain_Dairy_Cattle_2015/ baseline.

What you’ll edit

Category Files
User inputs (fill these in) livestock_census.csv · diet_profiles.csv · diet_ingredients.csv · ruminant_definitions.csv · livestock_weights.csv · manure_management.csv
Reference libraries (consult only) feed_characteristics.csv · mapping.csv · forages.parquet · fao_crops.parquet · ipcc_coefficients.csv · ipcc_mm.csv · ecoalim.parquet

Full details on every file above are in the Technical Reference vignette.

Step 1 — The Census (livestock_census.csv)

Open livestock_census.csv. This is where you define who is on the farm and in what row order you want cohorts displayed in output tables and charts. For this basic example, we work at national level, so subregion is left blank.

farm_id animal_tag region subregion population
farm_1 mature_dairy_cattle spain 848,686

Step 2 — Designing the Diet

The diet is filled in manually based on nutritional reports (e.g. Informe Zootécnico 2015).

A. Check available ingredients

Open feed_characteristics.csv to see the list of available feed items. You can also add new ingredients here, as long as every required column is filled in (see Adding a New Ingredient).

B. Define the profile — diet_profiles.csv

diet_tag forage_share concentrate_share milk_share milk_replacer_share
diet_dairy_mature 60 40 0 0

C. Ingredient breakdown — diet_ingredients.csv

Repeat the same diet_tag once per ingredient.

diet_tag ingredient_type ingredient ingredient_share country_of_origin custom_yield_kg_ha
diet_dairy_mature concentrate corn 44.85 spain NA
diet_dairy_mature concentrate soybean_meal_44_cp 17.12 NA NA
diet_dairy_mature concentrate rapeseed_meal_00_33_cp 28.71 NA 3200

✅ Shares sum to 100% within each category — ensure all ingredient_share values within concentrate and forage each total 100%.

🌍 Missing origins: leave country_of_origin as NA when you don’t know where a feed comes from. herdr resolves it automatically using FAO trade data — see Land Use Methodology for how.

🎯 Overriding the yield: custom_yield_kg_ha lets you skip the FAO/trade lookup entirely for a given ingredient. If you already know the real yield for your farm or region — e.g. 3200 kg DM/ha — enter it here and herdr uses that value directly for the land-use calculation.

Step 3 — Animal Categories and Coefficients (ruminant_definitions.csv)

Open ruminant_definitions.csv. This file classifies your cohort’s species (animal_type), production target (animal_subtype: strictly dairy or meat), and lifecycle role (production_role: strictly mature, replacement, or slaughter), and links it to the IPCC Tier 2 equations (cfi, ca, c, c_pregnancy_cattle in ipcc_coefficients.csv).

farm_id animal_tag region animal_type animal_subtype production_role diet_tag cfi ca c milk_yield_kg_year fat_content_pct protein_content_pct c_pregnancy_cattle pregnancy_rate replacement_rate
farm_1 mature_dairy_cattle spain cattle dairy mature diet_dairy_mature cattle_buffalo [lactating cows] stall females 8,894.38 3.73 3.39 cattle and buffalo 0.90 0.27

💡 Why replacement_rate = 0.27 matters even when automatic_cycle = FALSE:
In a dairy herd, 27% of mature cows are culled annually and sold for meat. herdr uses replacement_rate to compute annual culled cow carcass output (meat_carcass_weight_kg) and applies the IDF (2022) Net Energy physical allocation between milk (milk_FPCM_kg) and cull meat.

Step 4 — Body Weights (livestock_weights.csv)

Open livestock_weights.csv. Make sure the identifying keys match the census exactly.

farm_id animal_tag region adult_weight_kg productive_period_days initial_weight_kg final_weight_kg
farm_1 mature_dairy_cattle spain 675 365 675 675

ℹ️ About productive_period_days:
* For adult breeding females (except laying hens), this represents the inter-parturition interval in days (here, 365 days corresponds to an annual calving interval).
* For laying hens, it represents the commercial laying cycle duration until depopulation.
* For all other cohorts (growing, fattening, replacement), it represents their life cycle / life-stage duration (days on feed).

Step 5 — Manure Management (manure_management.csv)

  1. Check ipcc_mm.csv for valid system_base, system_variant, and climate_zone combinations — or browse the Manure System Guide.
  2. If a cohort splits its manure across more than one system, duplicate the row and divide the allocation between them so it sums to 1.0.
farm_id animal_tag region system_base system_variant management_months system_climate system_subclimate climate_zone climate_moisture b_0 allocation
farm_1 mature_dairy_cattle spain liquid_slurry with_natural_crust_cover 3 warm temperate zone_dry dry dairy_cattle_high_productivity 0.3
farm_1 mature_dairy_cattle spain solid_storage — — warm — — default dairy_cattle_high_productivity 0.7

Step 6 — Running the Analysis & Inspecting Outputs

Once every CSV above is complete, run the consolidated assessment from R:

library(herdr)

results <- generate_impact_assessment(
  automatic_cycle = FALSE,
  farm_country    = "Spain",
  year            = 2015,
  gwp_report      = "AR5"
)

# Table 1: Absolute GHG emissions (Gg CO2e), land (m2), water (m3), and per-head footprints
results$totals

# Table 2: Product intensities (per kg FPCM milk, per kg cull meat, per kg protein) & Protein FCR
results$intensities

# Visualize Milk Carbon Footprint (Scope 1 + Feed Fossil + Feed LUC per kg FPCM milk)
plot_herdr_results(
  df              = results,
  group_cols      = c("farm_id", "animal_tag"),
  func_name       = "generate_impact_assessment",
  impact_category = "ghg",
  functional_unit = "milk"
)
